The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources the PKGBUILD and reads metadata variables; it does not execute functions like `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, `check()`, or `package()`. In this PKGBUILD, all code at global scope consists of safe, declarative variable assignments (e.g., `pkgname`, `pkgdesc`, `source`, `sha256sums`) with no command substitutions, shell executions, or external downloads.

The `source` array uses a Git URL pointing to the declared upstream repository (`https://github.com/aravance/enclavectl.git`), which is appropriate for a `-git` package. The `sha256sums=('SKIP')` entry is expected for VCS-based packages and does not pose a risk during `--printsrcinfo`, as no sources are downloaded or verified at this stage. There are no top-level shell expansions or calls to `curl`, `wget`, `eval`, or other dangerous constructs that could trigger malicious behavior during sourcing.

Thus, simply parsing this PKGBUILD for metadata via `--printsrcinfo` poses no security risk.
</details>
